item.title: ODI Newsletter - April 12, 2024
item.description:
Share / View as a webpage

Join us for an exciting day of information and resources to enhance your supplier diversity and procurement opportunities! Attendees will have the opportunity to connect with governmental entities, industry leaders, entrepreneurs and professionals from various backgrounds.

This event will provide a variety of educational opportunities aimed at increasing supply chain sustainability and fostering inclusivity and collaboration in supplier diversity. It will also include information on a diverse range of funding opportunities and offer guidance on becoming certified.

Space is limited, so reserve your spot TODAY by scanning the QR code or visit https://www.bit.ly/2024SDPS. Stay tuned for more details to come! For more information, contact odi@columbus.gov.

Connect with Government Contracting Opportunities May 8-9 in Dayton

SAVE THE DATE!

The Ohio Business Matchmaker is back! Register now to attend May 8-9, 2024 at the Nutter Center in Dayton!

For a more than a decade, the Ohio Business Matchmaker has connected small businesses to government contracting opportunities. As one of the largest business to government matchmaking events in the state, this event offers a unique opportunity for businesses interested in doing business with the federal, state or local government to meet with representatives to market and sell their goods and services. This event is open to all businesses. Visit https://www.ohiobusinessmatchmaker.com/ 

Learn More & Register!

Have You Heard the Benefits of Being City of Columbus MBE or WBE Certified?

Your business has direct access to exclusive City of Columbus contract opportunities for City of Columbus Certified MBE/WBEs!  In fact, we even have incentives and other ways to improve economic impact and increase diversity spend!  Find out about the City of Columbus Supplier Diversity Program and MBE/WBE Goal initiatives!

Get certified with our array of free certifications. If eligible for multiple certifications, stack them by selecting all that apply to your business!

Visit the Office of Diversity & Inclusion Website

Construction Prequalification

Are You Prepared to Bid on City of Columbus Construction Work?

Construction prequalification is required for construction contracts that exceed $500,000.  If your firm performs construction related work, you must submit an application to get prequalified for General Contractors and Licensed Construction Trade Subcontractors in the following trades:

♦ Heating

♦ Ventilating & Air Conditioning

♦ Refrigeration

♦ Electrical

♦ Plumbing Hydronic

♦ Fire Protection/Firefighting Equipment

Website: https://www.columbus.gov/finance/financial-management-group/Office-of-Construction-Prequalification/

Email: prequalification@columbus.gov

Please allow 30 calendar days from the date of receipt
for application processing

Follow the 3-Step Process to Register to Do Business and Complete the On-Line Certification Application!

Vendors must register on the Vendor Services portal before doing business with the City of Columbus and becoming Minority or Women Business Enterprise (MBE/WBE) certified. 

Register Here!

After registration, you will receive an email to complete the required Contract Compliance Questionnaire. Vendors must be contract compliant in order to do business with Columbus.

Get Compliant!

In the Diversity Compliance Portal, you can complete the online certification application, track the status of your application and receive a copy of your certification approval letter.

Get Certified!

For more certification information or questions, contact us at: DiversityCertifications@columbus.gov

  • Environmental Management, Refuse Disposal and Treatment

Access valuable tools, secure funding opportunities, and connect through networking channels. Explore the range of resources tailored to support your entrepreneurial journey at https://cbussmallbizhub.com/

Visit The Small Biz Hub

Vendor Profile Information | Search for MBE/WBEs

Are You a City Certified Business & Need to Enhance Your Vendor Profile?

You can boost your profile by adding branding, services, capabilities, references, past performance and more!  Adding commodity codes based on the products, services and capabilities you provide helps businesses better locate you!  Not sure where to find codes?  Use the NAICS search available here:  https://www.naics.com/search/

Is Your Business Certification Up to Date? Update Your Profile

You don’t have to be in Renewal Status to update your vendor profile or certification documents. Update your profile with new capabilities, required documents or ownership changes as soon as you receive them.  Expired certifications can result in delayed opportunities to grow your business.

Searching for a City of Columbus Certified MBE/WBE Business?

Access the Diverse Business Directory online with key-word search capabilities to find certified vendors ready to do business!

Search the Online Directory

COMTO Columbus Scholarship Application - DEADLINE APRIL 12, 2024

COMTO Columbus provides a networking forum for minority professionals, which includes a broad and growing membership of individuals in all multi-modal agencies, large and small corporations, historically underutilized businesses, state departments of transportation, academic institutions and other non-profit organizations.  Our core values are reflected in our commitments to Advocacy, Diversity & Inclusion, Education & Scholarship, Integrity and Service.

If you are or know of a college student (traditional or adult) in need of a scholarship, apply for this opportunity for educational funding for historically underrepresented minority groups! Whether you’re planning a career in transportation or any STEAM related activities, this may be the scholarship opportunity for you!
Click Here To Learn More & Apply

ECDI is dedicated to assuring every entrepreneur – regardless of where they came from, where they live, their gender or their race – has access to funding and business mentoring services they need to build a business that thrives.

Construction Startup Cohort: Deadline to Apply is Friday, April 19th at 12 p.m.

Building a solid foundation in the construction industry is essential, but if you want your budding construction business to be successful, it’s crucial to understand the business side of things.

Led by industry experts, the Construction Startup Cohort bridges this gap by providing aspiring entrepreneurs with a comprehensive program that covers everything from business planning to strategic management in just 11 weeks! Curriculum Highlights include Business Planning, Market Research, Financial Statements & Operations Management Essentials. Visit and apply at https://www.ecdi.org/mcrc-cohort to give your business a solid foundation.

​ Important dates:

  • Application Deadline: Friday, April 19 at 12:00 p.m.
  • ​​Cohort Schedule: 5:30 - 7:00 p.m. on Thursdays starting April 25.

​Please note, courses will take place at ECDI's Columbus office at
1655 Old Leonard Ave, Columbus, OH 43219.
Learn More & Apply

Industry Insight Sessions: Professional Services Available for MCRC Clients

The Minority Contractor Resource Center (MCRC) strives to empowers MBEs for growth by providing comprehensive support, including business training, coaching, networking and procurement opportunities. Sessions offered cover various topics such as plain reading, estimation, project management, sales, business development, contractor prequalification, preconstruction & more!

If you are interested in access these services and learning from our expert volunteers, please complete the MCRC Professional Service Request Form.

MCRC Request Form

Thursday, April 18 | MWBE and EDGE Night with Gilbane Building Company

Join Gilbane Building Company at Columbus Downtown High School on April 18 for a special networking event for Minority and Women Business Enterprises (M/WBE) and EDGE businesses. The event highlights Gilbane's commitment to diversity and connecting with M/WBE and EDGE partners.

The event will be held from 4:30 PM to 6:30 p.m. and will feature a discussion of exciting projects like Intel Ohio One and The Merchant Building. It's a prime opportunity for diverse businesses to meet the Gilbane team, learn about upcoming ventures, and explore potential collaborations.

Register to attend at https://tinyurl.com/yz4ubthn.

item.title: Mid-Year Diversity Performance Metrics
item.description:
Diversity Performance Metrics

The Office of Diversity and Inclusion is pleased to present the 2022 Comprehensive Diversity and Inclusion Dashboard. As a city, we are laser focused on advancing the Mayor’s Equity Agenda. The combined dashboard provides at-a-glance, a quarterly snapshot of the diversity metrics for the City of Columbus. These tools are provided to elevate our strategic focus on diversity, equity and inclusion within the City of Columbus workforce and supply chains. The enclosed reports represent the collective efforts of the Office of Diversity and Inclusion and each of the city department toward making the City of Columbus a more inclusive and equitable community in which to live and thrive. Thank you to Mayor Andrew J. Ginther for your vision, leadership, and commitment to creating “America’s Equal Opportunity City.”

SUPPLIER DIVERSITY

To explore the City of Columbus’ Supplier Diversity Data, please click here. (must be on the city's network to access this link)

  • 2022 Preliminary City Utilization is 10.036%. Due to bidding delays in the first half of the year, utilization is lower than normal. We expect utilization to improve in the second half.
  • Launched the LGBTBE Certification Program.

WORKFORCE DIVERSITY

To explore the City of Columbus’ Workforce Diversity Data, please click here.

  • Govern 2.0 Symposium October 6, 2022 at Vue Columbus. Register here.
  • Graduated first cohort of the Diversity Youth Entrepreneur Program (DYEP).
